name: Al-Qiyāmah
blurb: An argument in miniature: if God can reassemble your fingertips, the Day you keep postponing is not the hard part.

words.root: √q-s-m — dividing, allotting, settling a matter by portions
words.meaning: I swear / I take an oath
words.magic: The surah opens on an oath rather than a claim, so the reader is inside a sworn statement before a single argument has been made.
words.grammar: Form IV present verb, first person singular.
words.why: The present tense makes it a standing oath rather than a one-off — it renews every time the verse is recited.
words.note: Present tense = a living, renewed oath.

words.root: √l-w-m — blame, reproach, holding someone to account
words.magic: God swears by your guilty conscience — the nagging voice inside you is offered as evidence that a reckoning exists.
words.grammar: Intensive adjective on the faʿʿālah pattern, feminine, in the genitive after the oath.
words.why: The faʿʿālah pattern means one who does it constantly, not once in a while.
words.note: Intensive form = a soul on constant self-audit.

words.root: √ḥ-s-b — counting, reckoning, calculating a total
words.magic: The question is the argument. It makes the denier hear his own assumption spoken out loud, where it sounds much thinner.
words.grammar: Interrogative hamzah + present verb; a rhetorical question expecting “no.”
words.why: Ḥasiba is reckoning that turns out wrong — supposing, not knowing.
words.note: A denying question: “does he really think so?”

words.root: √ʿ-ẓ-m — greatness, magnitude; and bones, the body's great frame
words.magic: The objection is quoted at its strongest before it is answered — scattered bones, the hardest case anyone could put.
words.grammar: Broken plural, accusative as the object of “gather.”
words.why: Bones are what survives and what scatters — the exact part that makes resurrection sound impossible.
words.note: The hardest remains — so the strongest resurrection challenge.

words.root: √q-d-r — power joined to exact measure
words.magic: The answer arrives before the objection has finished landing — “yes,” then immediately something harder than what was asked.
words.grammar: Active participle, plural, accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl).
words.why: Qādir is settled, standing capability, not a burst of effort.
words.note: Power here means strength plus precision.

words.root: √s-w-y — making even, proportioning, levelling into shape
words.magic: The reply overshoots the challenge on purpose: not merely bones reassembled, but fingertips re-formed.
words.grammar: Form II present verb, subjunctive after an.
words.why: Form II carries careful, repeated shaping — craftsmanship, not assembly.
words.note: Form II = careful, exact crafting.

words.root: √b-n-n — the finger-ends, the tips
words.magic: Of everything in a body, the verse picks the one surface that is unique to you — and modern readers hear fingerprints in it.
words.grammar: Collective noun with attached pronoun, accusative object.
words.why: The fingertip is the smallest, most individual detail — so it settles the argument by excess.
words.note: From bones to fingerprints — re-creation down to the ridges.

words.root: √f-j-r — splitting, bursting open, breaking a barrier
words.magic: The verse exposes the real motive under the denial: he does not doubt the Day, he wants the road ahead of him clear.
words.grammar: Present verb, subjunctive after the lām of purpose.
words.why: Fajara is tearing an opening, not slipping — deliberate, not accidental.
words.note: Brazen, barrier-breaking sin.

words.root: √ʾ-m-m — front, forward, that which leads
words.magic: One word holds both his open calendar and the Day closing in on it — the future he is counting on is the thing coming for him.
words.grammar: Adverb of place with attached pronoun.
words.why: It says in front of, not later — the Day is approaching, not merely scheduled.
words.note: Can mean both his future and the Day ahead.

words.root: An interrogative reserved for weighty, dreaded times
words.magic: The sneer is preserved in the grammar — the questioner is not asking for a date, he is mocking the idea of one.
words.grammar: Interrogative of time, used adverbially.
words.why: Ayyāna rather than matā: it is kept for momentous, feared appointments.
words.note: Used for a grave, dreaded appointment.

words.root: √b-r-q — flashing, lightning, a dazzling glare
words.magic: The scene is told in past-tense verbs although it is still future — the Day is reported as something already done.
words.grammar: Perfect verb, third person masculine singular.
words.why: The lightning verb is applied to the eye itself, so the panic is seen from inside the skull.
words.note: Panic strikes the eye like a blinding flash.

words.root: √kh-s-f — sinking, being swallowed, losing one's light
words.magic: The Qur'an reaches for the technical word an astronomer would use, so the cosmic collapse is described with precision rather than noise.
words.grammar: Perfect verb, third person masculine singular.
words.why: Khusūf is the moon's own eclipse-word — kusūf belongs to the sun.
words.note: The moon's own precise eclipse-verb.

words.root: √f-r-r — fleeing, bolting away
words.magic: He no longer asks whether the Day is real — he asks which way out. The argument is over; only the panic is left.
words.grammar: Noun of place (ism makān) with the definite article.
words.why: It names a place, not an act — he is scanning for an exit that has to exist somewhere.
words.note: The desperate search for an exit.

words.root: √w-z-r — a burden; and the mountain crag you shelter behind
words.magic: The word for the heaviest thing you carry is also the word for the safest place to hide — and the verse denies you it.
words.grammar: Indefinite noun, subject of the negation lā.
words.why: It pictures the strongest shelter an Arabian imagination could reach for, then removes it.
words.note: Not even a mountain-like shelter exists.

words.root: √q-r-r — settling, coming to rest, becoming fixed
words.magic: Immediately after “no refuge,” the true destination is named — there is nowhere to run because there is somewhere to arrive.
words.grammar: Form X noun of place, subject of the sentence.
words.why: Form X carries seeking to settle — this is where the running finally stops.
words.note: The only true stopping-place is with your Lord.

words.root: √n-b-ʾ — news of consequence, a weighty report
words.magic: He is told about himself. He does not testify, defend or narrate — his own life is read back to him.
words.grammar: Passive Form II present verb.
words.why: Nabaʾ is heavy news, and Form II makes it itemized rather than summarized.
words.note: Form II suggests detailed disclosure, item by item.

words.root: √q-d-m — going forward, putting something in front
words.magic: Deeds are pictured as luggage shipped forward to a destination you have not reached yet.
words.grammar: Form II perfect verb.
words.why: Form II means he pushed it forward himself — nobody sent it for him.
words.note: What a person put forward in deeds.

words.root: √ʾ-kh-r — delaying, holding back, leaving behind
words.magic: Paired with qaddama, the two verbs close a complete ledger: what he sent forward and what he left in his wake. Nothing falls between them.
words.grammar: Form II perfect verb, the exact antonym pattern of the previous word.
words.why: It covers the sins of omission and the traces that outlive him, not only what he actively did.
words.note: What he neglected, or left as traces after him.

words.root: √b-ṣ-r — seeing, perceiving, clear evidence
words.magic: The verse does not say he has evidence against himself — it says he is evidence. The witness stand and the accused are the same person.
words.grammar: Intensive feminine noun used as the predicate.
words.why: Baṣīra means both insight and proof, so self-knowledge becomes testimony.
words.note: The soul itself testifies against the person.

words.root: √ʿ-dh-r — excusing, clearing oneself of blame
words.magic: The plural does the work: he does not offer one explanation, he throws every excuse he owns, and none of them lands.
words.grammar: Broken plural with attached pronoun, accusative.
words.why: Maʿdhirah is a formal plea, which keeps the courtroom image intact.
words.note: Flimsy self-justifications cannot save him.

words.root: √ḥ-r-k — movement, stirring, setting in motion
words.magic: In the middle of a terror scene the voice turns aside to one man, quietly, about his tongue — and then returns. The intimacy is the point.
words.grammar: Form II present verb, jussive after the prohibitive lā.
words.why: Form II fits small repeated motion — the lips hurrying to keep up.
words.note: A command not to rush the revelation.

words.root: √t-b-ʿ — following, coming behind
words.magic: The instruction is a whole method of learning: receive first, repeat second. Anxiety to hold on is answered with a promise to hold it for you.
words.grammar: Form VIII imperative.
words.why: It means follow behind, not run alongside — the order matters.
words.note: Follow the Qur'an's recitation — listen first, repeat after.

words.root: √b-y-n — becoming clear, separating out until distinct
words.magic: God takes responsibility not only for the words but for their meaning — the text and its explanation come from the same source.
words.grammar: Verbal noun with attached pronoun, accusative.
words.why: Bayān is making a thing shine clear, stronger than merely explaining it.
words.note: Allah guarantees its explanation.

words.root: √ʿ-j-l — haste, hurry, wanting it now
words.meaning: the fleeting world / the immediate one
words.magic: The world is named by its speed rather than its pleasure — the diagnosis is in the noun before any criticism is made.
words.grammar: Active participle used as a noun, accusative object.
words.why: It says the attraction out loud: dunya is loved because it is near and quick, not because it is good.
words.note: Dunya is loved because it feels quick and near.

words.root: √w-dh-r — leaving something behind, letting it go untended
words.magic: Not “you deny the Hereafter” but “you leave it” — which is exactly how most people actually lose it.
words.grammar: Present verb, second person masculine plural.
words.why: Wadhara is abandoning and walking on, a quieter and truer charge than denial.
words.note: Used for abandoning the Hereafter.

words.root: √n-ḍ-r — freshness, bloom, the glow of a well-watered plant
words.magic: The reward is described as a change in the face before anything is said about gardens — bliss shows up on the skin.
words.grammar: Active participle, feminine singular.
words.why: Naḍāra is the freshness of green growth, so the joy reads as living, not painted on.
words.note: Faces lit up with joy and bliss.

words.root: √n-ẓ-r — looking, gazing, directing the eye
words.magic: The most famous sound-play in the surah: nāḍira and nāẓira differ by a single dot, and the glow is explained by what the eyes are turned toward.
words.grammar: Active participle, feminine singular, same pattern as the previous word.
words.why: Naẓara ilā is to look at something directly — and here the object is their Lord.
words.note: One letter changes the meaning from glow to gaze.

words.root: √b-s-r — grimness, a face pulled tight and sour
words.magic: The other group is drawn on the same participle pattern, so the contrast is exact — two faces, one word-shape, opposite weather.
words.grammar: Active participle, feminine singular.
words.why: Basara is the look that arrives before the blow does — dread, not yet pain.
words.note: Faces darkened by dread.

words.root: √f-q-r — the vertebrae; breaking the spine
words.magic: The disaster is not described, only what it does to a body — the Qur'an names the injury and lets you supply the event.
words.grammar: Active participle used as a noun, feminine.
words.why: From faqār, the vertebra: it is the one word for a blow you cannot stand up after.
words.note: A disaster that feels spine-snapping.

words.root: From tarquwah — the collarbone
words.magic: The camera drops from cosmic collapse to one bedside detail: a soul arriving at the notch of the throat.
words.grammar: Broken plural of tarquwah, accusative.
words.why: Naming the exact bone makes the moment of death physical and observed, not abstract.
words.note: The soul reaches the throat at death.

words.root: √r-q-y — rising, ascending; and reciting words of healing
words.meaning: a healer / one who can cure?
words.magic: The room asks for anyone who can save him while the angels ask who will take him up — one word carries both questions at once.
words.grammar: Active participle, indefinite, of a defective (manqūṣ) root.
words.why: The double sense is deliberate: the same letters serve the panic below and the ascent above.
words.note: A deliberate double meaning: healer, and the one who ascends with the soul.

words.root: √f-r-q — separating, parting into two
words.magic: He spent a life certain of nothing; now, too late, the verse says he knows.
words.grammar: Verbal noun with the definite article, subject of the clause.
words.why: Firāq is the parting of two things that were joined — soul from body, man from world, in one word.
words.note: The dying person knows it is the final separation.

words.root: √l-f-f — wrapping, twisting, winding around
words.magic: Distress is drawn as physical entanglement — the troubles do not queue up, they knot together.
words.grammar: Form VIII perfect verb, feminine singular.
words.why: Iltaffa is twisting into one another, not merely touching.
words.note: One distress folds into another.

words.root: √s-w-q — the shin, the leg one stands on
words.magic: “Shin against shin” — the body's own posture becomes the measure of the agony, with no adjective needed.
words.grammar: Noun, nominative, in the idiom sāq bi-sāq.
words.why: The shin is what carries you; when it is bound to the other, movement is over.
words.note: Leg upon leg — mounting agony.

words.root: √s-w-q — driving, herding, leading a flock onward
words.magic: The scene's last word is driving. The man who walked wherever he pleased is now moved like livestock.
words.grammar: Verbal noun / noun of place from the same root as al-sāq.
words.why: Sawq is the driving of a herd — direction chosen by someone else.
words.note: All are driven onward to their Lord.

words.root: √ṣ-d-q — truth, sincerity, holding something to be true
words.magic: The indictment is built from what he did not do inside himself — no belief, no prayer — before it reaches anything he did.
words.grammar: Form II perfect verb, negated.
words.why: Ṣaddaqa is inner assent, not lip agreement — the exact thing that was absent.
words.note: Inner assent to truth was the thing missing.

words.root: √w-l-y — turning; nearness, allegiance, taking a side
words.magic: The root that means drawing near is used for walking off — the same word family holds both the loyalty offered and the loyalty refused.
words.grammar: Form V perfect verb.
words.why: Form V makes it reflexive and deliberate: he turned himself away.
words.note: A deliberate turning of the back.

words.root: √m-ṭ-ṭ — stretching out, drawing oneself long
words.magic: After the theology, the surah convicts him by his walk — the strut back to his people is the last evidence entered.
words.grammar: Form V present verb, of a defective root.
words.why: It pictures a body stretched tall with self-satisfaction — arrogance made visible.
words.note: Arrogance shows up in how he walks.

words.root: √w-l-y — nearness; here, doom drawing near
words.magic: The phrase is fired twice, then twice again — the threat does not escalate in vocabulary, only in repetition, which is worse.
words.grammar: Elative form used as a fixed threat idiom.
words.why: It is the language of a street warning, not a sermon — nearer, and nearer.
words.note: A threat-idiom, repeated for rising doom.

words.root: √s-d-y — left loose, untended, running free like unherded cattle
words.magic: The whole case for accountability rests on one small word for “loose” — you were never released without a purpose.
words.grammar: Indefinite noun in the accusative as a circumstantial state (ḥāl).
words.why: Sudan is the animal nobody watches and nobody claims — precisely what a human is not.
words.note: Man was not created without purpose.

words.root: √n-ṭ-f — dripping, trickling, a single drop
words.magic: Having argued forward to the Day, the surah now argues backward to the drop — the same power, running the other direction.
words.grammar: Indefinite noun, accusative.
words.why: Nutfa is not a quantity but a drip — the smallest possible beginning for the largest possible claim.
words.note: The resurrection proof starts from the humblest origin.

words.root: √m-n-y — measuring out, decreeing; and the fluid itself
words.magic: The same letters that mean “to apportion by decree” name the fluid — origin and destiny share a root.
words.grammar: Noun in the genitive after min.
words.why: It quietly repeats the surah's thesis: nothing about you was left to chance.
words.note: Even the origin is divinely measured.

words.root: √m-n-y — pouring forth, emitting
words.magic: The verb is passive, so the man is not the actor even at his own beginning — he is what happened, not who did it.
words.grammar: Passive present verb, third person, of a defective root.
words.why: The passive removes him from the sentence exactly where he imagines himself in charge.
words.note: Passive form — man is acted upon, not in control.

words.root: √ʿ-l-q — clinging, hanging on, attaching
words.magic: Each stage of becoming a person gets exactly one word — the speed of the telling matches the speed of the change.
words.grammar: Indefinite noun, accusative.
words.why: ʿAlaqa names the behaviour, not the appearance: the thing that clings to the wall.
words.note: The whole embryo stage captured in one root.

words.root: √s-w-y — making even, proportioning
words.magic: The same verb used back in verse 4 for re-forming the fingertips returns here for forming you the first time — the argument closes its own circle.
words.grammar: Form II perfect verb, of a defective root.
words.why: Using the identical root twice is the proof: the second making is the first making, repeated.
words.note: The One who first fashioned can refashion.

words.root: √z-w-j — pairing, mating, joining two into a set
words.magic: From one drop come two kinds — the unity of the origin and the duality of the outcome sit in the same sentence.
words.grammar: Dual noun, accusative.
words.why: Zawj is not simply “one of two” but each half of a matched pair — neither is complete alone.
words.note: Complementary duality from one origin.

words.root: √dh-k-r — the male; and, in its other sense, remembrance
words.magic: The pair is spelled out rather than left implied, so the claim is concrete: this specific outcome, from that specific drop.
words.grammar: Noun, accusative, standing in apposition (badal) to “the two mates.”
words.why: Naming both halves individually keeps the verse from becoming an abstraction.
words.note: One half of the created pair.

words.root: √ʾ-n-th — the female
words.magic: Two words, one conjunction, and the entire diversity of humankind is accounted for from a single fluid.
words.grammar: Noun, accusative, the second half of the apposition.
words.why: It completes the pair, so the design argument is finished rather than half-stated.
words.note: The paired opposite completing humankind.

words.root: √ḥ-y-y — life, living, being made alive
words.magic: The surah ends where it began — with a question — but this time the reader has been handed everything needed to answer it.
words.grammar: Form IV present verb, subjunctive after an.
words.why: Form IV is causing life, not merely being alive — the exact act under dispute.
words.note: The final question pushes the listener to say yes.

words.root: √m-w-t — death, the dead
words.magic: The last word of the argument is the objection itself — the surah lets the hardest fact have the final position and still wins.
words.grammar: Broken plural, accusative object.
words.why: Placing “the dead” at the end leaves the reader holding the question, not the answer.
words.note: Life versus death seals the surah's argument.

name: Al-Mursalāt
blurb: Five oaths of moving air, then one refrain struck ten times like a bell: woe, that Day, to the deniers.

words.root: √r-s-l — sending forth smoothly, dispatching in sequence
words.meaning: those sent out one after another — classically understood as the winds, and by some as angels sent on mission
words.magic: The passive participle keeps the spotlight on the One who sends them, while the plural oath opening creates motion from the very first word.
words.grammar: Passive participle; sound feminine plural.
words.why: It suggests directed sending, not random movement.
words.note: Same family as risālah — a message being sent.

words.root: √ʿ-r-f — something recognized, ordered, familiar; also used for a horse's mane in successive strands
words.meaning: in ordered succession, one after another
words.magic: It gives the oath a sense of orderly ranks, or winds coming in recognizable waves.
words.grammar: Accusative adverbial expression describing the manner of the sending.
words.why: It adds order and continuity, not chaos.
words.note: Picture wave after wave, like neat strands of a mane.

words.root: √ʿ-ṣ-f — violent blasting, stormy force
words.magic: The sound and the sense both feel forceful — the oath rises from orderly sending to powerful sweeping.
words.grammar: Active participle; sound feminine plural.
words.why: It is stronger than a plain word for blowing; it means a storm-like blast.
words.note: Think of a wind so strong it whips everything aside.

words.root: The same √ʿ-ṣ-f field of violent scattering and storm-force
words.magic: Pairing the participle with its verbal noun intensifies the action: not merely “blowing,” but “blowing with full force.”
words.grammar: Verbal noun in the accusative, reinforcing the manner and intensity.
words.why: It piles emphasis onto the previous oath word.
words.note: The same root twice means the storm is really storming.

words.root: √n-sh-r — spreading out, unfolding, scattering wide
words.magic: After the stormy force comes wide spreading — as if the air opens and disperses what was packed together.
words.grammar: Active participle; sound feminine plural.
words.why: It gives a sense of opening out over a wide range.
words.note: Think of a folded cloth being opened and spread.

words.root: The same √n-sh-r field of spreading and unfolding
words.magic: Like ʿāṣifāt / ʿaṣfan before it, the pair strengthens the motion and makes the sequence vivid.
words.grammar: Verbal noun in the accusative for emphasis.
words.why: It turns the image from a simple action into an all-out dispersal.
words.note: نَشَرَ is like opening and spreading pages across a table.

words.root: √f-r-q — separating, distinguishing, making a clear difference
words.magic: The surah moves from motion in nature to separation and sorting — a perfect lead-in to revelation and judgment.
words.grammar: Active participle; sound feminine plural.
words.why: It suggests clear distinction, not vague difference.
words.note: Same family as furqān — truth being separated from falsehood.

words.root: The same √f-r-q field of cutting apart and distinguishing
words.magic: The maṣdar adds force: this separation is sharp and unmistakable.
words.grammar: Verbal noun in the accusative, intensifying the act.
words.why: It turns “separating” into “separating with full decisiveness.”
words.note: فَرْق = a line drawn clearly between two sides.

words.root: √l-q-y — to cast, throw, deliver, or convey something so it reaches its target
words.meaning: those that cast down or deliver the reminder
words.magic: After sending, blasting, spreading and separating, the sequence lands at revelation being delivered.
words.grammar: Active participle; sound feminine plural.
words.why: It suggests precise delivery, not a vague arrival.
words.note: Think of a messenger placing an important letter exactly where it must land.

words.root: √dh-k-r — remembering, mentioning, bringing something to mind
words.magic: Revelation is called dhikr because it wakes up what the heart should already remember.
words.grammar: Verbal noun in the accusative.
words.why: It is not just information but a reminder that stirs memory and awareness.
words.note: Dhikr is what pulls a forgotten truth back into your mind.

words.root: √ʿ-dh-r = excuse, clearing blame; √n-dh-r = warning, alerting to danger
words.meaning: as excuse and as warning — revelation leaves no one able to say “I never knew”
words.magic: The pair covers both sides: truth excuses the sincere and warns the stubborn.
words.grammar: Two accusative verbal nouns, paired for balance.
words.why: Together they show revelation completes the proof.
words.note: One removes excuse; the other rings the alarm.

words.root: √w-q-t — time, timing, fixing an appointed moment
words.meaning: the messengers were assigned to a fixed time
words.magic: Everything in the surah moves toward a scheduled final appointment.
words.grammar: Passive Form II perfect; feminine singular agreeing with rusul as a non-human plural.
words.why: It emphasizes appointment and precision, not randomness.
words.note: Same family as waqt — a time set on a calendar.

words.root: √ʾ-j-l — term, deadline, postponement, appointed limit
words.magic: Suspense rises — the Day was not canceled, only held to its appointed time.
words.grammar: Passive Form II perfect.
words.why: It signals postponement with purpose, not absence.
words.note: An exam date can be postponed, but it still comes.

words.root: √f-ṣ-l — separation, decisive cutting apart, making a matter clear
words.meaning: the Day of Decision / Separation — truth from falsehood, believers from deniers
words.magic: The surah's opening “separating” words culminate here in the ultimate separation.
words.grammar: Iḍāfa phrase: “day of the separation / decision.”
words.why: Faṣl means a decisive final sorting, not a vague judgment.
words.note: This is the day every mixed-up case gets separated into its proper file.

words.root: √k-sh-ṭ — to strip off, peel back, pull away a covering
words.magic: The sky is pictured like a cover being peeled back — a dramatic unveiling.
words.grammar: Passive perfect, feminine singular.
words.why: It makes cosmic collapse feel visual and physical.
words.note: Imagine a sheet being yanked off the ceiling of the world.

words.root: √n-s-f — to blow away, scatter, uproot thoroughly
words.magic: Mountains — symbols of stability — are turned into something removable.
words.grammar: Passive perfect, feminine singular for the non-human plural subject.
words.why: It shows total uprooting, not mere shaking.
words.note: Even mountains get swept off the table.

words.root: A word of ruin, woe, and threatening doom
words.magic: Its repetition becomes the surah's drumbeat.
words.grammar: Indefinite noun used for terrifying force.
words.why: It is short, heavy and memorable — perfect as a refrain.
words.note: Every time the refrain hits, it lands like a warning bell.

words.root: √k-dh-b — lying, calling something false, rejecting truth
words.meaning: those who deny and call the message a lie
words.magic: The surah's refrain targets not mere doubters but active deniers.
words.grammar: Active participle plural, Form II sense.
words.why: It points to people who brand truth as false.
words.note: Not just “unconvinced” — they stamp the truth with “lie.”

words.root: √h-l-k — destruction, perishing, ruin
words.magic: The past nations are used as evidence for future judgment.
words.grammar: Form IV verb from ahlaka.
words.why: It carries complete ruin, not a small punishment.
words.note: The Qur'an often points backward in history so you fear what lies ahead.

words.root: first / last · earlier / later
words.meaning: the former peoples and the later peoples
words.magic: The pairing sweeps across history — nobody escapes the pattern.
words.grammar: Two plural adjectives used as nouns.
words.why: The pair covers all generations, early and late.
words.note: Old nations are not museum pieces; later ones can follow the same path.

words.root: √t-b-ʿ — following, coming after, making something follow
words.meaning: We make the later ones follow them
words.magic: History is shown as a chain of consequences.
words.grammar: Form IV present verb with object pronoun.
words.why: It means causing one group to follow another in fate.
words.note: One line of deniers follows another like dominoes.

words.root: √kh-l-q — creating, shaping, bringing into existence with proportion
words.magic: The argument shifts from destroyed nations to your own creation.
words.grammar: Present verb with direct object pronoun “you.”
words.why: Creation itself becomes proof of accountability.
words.note: The One who made you can surely judge you.

words.root: māʾ = water; √m-h-n = lowly, slight, humble
words.meaning: a humble fluid — the human origin
words.magic: Arrogance is crushed by reminding man of his tiny beginning.
words.grammar: Noun + adjective phrase in the genitive.
words.why: Mahīn humbles human pride.
words.note: Proud man began as a drop.

words.root: √q-r-r = settling, resting; √m-k-n = firmness, stability, secure placement
words.meaning: a secure lodging place — the womb
words.magic: Your first home was hidden, settled and protected.
words.grammar: Noun + adjective phrase in the genitive.
words.why: It gives both rest and security in two compact words.
words.note: Before walking the earth, you were settled in a silent, secure room.

words.root: √q-d-r — measuring, decreeing, determining with exactness, and having power
words.magic: The same root carries both exact measure and full ability.
words.grammar: Perfect verb, first person plural.
words.why: It shows creation is precise, not accidental.
words.note: Qadar means nothing about you was thrown together.

words.root: The able, fully capable ones — from the same √q-d-r field
words.meaning: those perfectly able — here, God speaking in majesty
words.magic: Measure and power meet in one root family.
words.grammar: Active participle plural.
words.why: Ability here means precise power, not brute force alone.
words.note: The One who measures exactly is the One fully able.

words.root: √k-f-t — gathering, enclosing, holding things together
words.meaning: a place that gathers and contains — the earth
words.magic: Earth holds both the living on top and the dead within.
words.grammar: Accusative noun, complement to “We made the earth.”
words.why: It captures the earth as a container and collector.
words.note: The earth is a giant cradle above and a giant chamber below.

words.root: life and death
words.magic: One earth gathers both, making the scene broad and sobering.
words.grammar: Two accusative plurals paired in balance.
words.why: The pair shows the earth's total embrace.
words.note: The same ground carries footsteps and graves.

words.root: √r-s-w — firm anchoring, staying fixed, like a ship moored in place
words.magic: Mountains are pictured as stabilizers of the earth.
words.grammar: Broken plural used as object of “placed.”
words.why: It highlights steadiness, not just height.
words.note: Mountains are like pegs or anchors holding the scene steady.

words.root: √sh-m-kh — rising high, towering proudly
words.magic: Paired with rawāsi, the mountains are both stable and high.
words.grammar: Feminine sound plural adjective.
words.why: It adds vertical majesty to firmness.
words.note: These are not small hills; they lift their heads high.

words.root: Sweet, pleasant, easy to drink
words.magic: After mountains comes water — stability and mercy together.
words.grammar: Accusative adjective describing water.
words.why: Not just drinkable water, but delightfully sweet water.
words.note: Furāt is the opposite of bitter and salty — water you want to keep drinking.

words.root: √ṭ-l-q — setting out, being released, moving off decisively
words.meaning: Go on! Move toward what you used to deny
words.magic: A sharp command launches the scene into punishment.
words.grammar: Imperative plural, Form VII sense.
words.why: It gives force and momentum.
words.note: Once judgment starts, the command sends them straight onward.

words.root: √sh-ʿ-b — branching, splitting into divisions
words.meaning: branches or columns — in the phrase “three branching columns” of smoke
words.magic: The smoke is not one solid shelter but divided, deceptive layers.
words.grammar: Plural noun in the genitive after dhī.
words.why: It makes the image segmented and eerie.
words.note: Three branches of smoke, but none of them truly protects.

words.root: √ẓ-l-l — shade, shelter, cool cover
words.magic: The verse denies it — this is a “shade” that gives no real shade.
words.grammar: Adjective in the genitive after lā.
words.why: It sharpens the irony of false shelter.
words.note: A cloud of smoke that looks like shade but fails when you need it.

words.root: √sh-r-r — sparks or fiery fragments flung off
words.magic: The punishment is pictured through flying pieces, not just a single flame.
words.grammar: Singular collective noun in the genitive.
words.why: It shows danger multiplying and flying outward.
words.note: Not one flame — showers of fiery fragments.

words.root: √q-ṣ-r — a large structure, palace, or huge trunk-like mass
words.meaning: like massive palaces — describing the size of the sparks
words.magic: A spark is normally tiny; this simile makes it shockingly huge.
words.grammar: Preposition kāf for simile + noun in the genitive.
words.why: It exaggerates size in a vivid, unforgettable way.
words.note: The sparks are as if buildings are being thrown.

words.root: jimālah = camels; ṣufr = yellowish
words.meaning: like yellow camels — another simile for the sparks; some explain it as thick yellow ropes
words.magic: The verse stacks one simile after another for motion, colour and size.
words.grammar: Plural noun + plural adjective phrase.
words.why: Camels give a familiar desert image of long, moving, swaying shapes.
words.note: Giant yellow camel-like streaks of fire.

words.root: √n-ṭ-q — speaking, articulating, making words come out
words.magic: The deniers who once talked back are now mute.
words.grammar: Negated present plural verb.
words.why: Speechlessness shows helplessness.
words.note: Arguments disappear when the final truth arrives.

words.root: √ʾ-dh-n — permission, allowing, authorization
words.meaning: no permission will be given to them
words.magic: Not only do they not speak — they are not even allowed to speak.
words.grammar: Passive present verb with indirect object.
words.why: It intensifies helplessness from silence to barred speech.
words.note: The courtroom is so final they do not even get the floor.

words.root: √k-y-d — planning, plotting, arranging a scheme
words.magic: The challenge is sarcastic — “if you have a plan, use it now.”
words.grammar: Verbal noun / noun.
words.why: It exposes the emptiness of human scheming before divine judgment.
words.note: All clever plots run out of road at the Last Day.

words.root: √w-q-y — guarding, shielding, protecting yourself
words.meaning: the God-conscious, those who guarded themselves through taqwā
words.magic: After many refrains of warning, the surah opens a cool garden scene for the protected ones.
words.grammar: Plural active participle, Form VIII sense.
words.why: Taqwā is protective, like building a shield between yourself and harm.
words.note: A muttaqī is someone who lives with a spiritual shield up.

words.root: shade and springs
words.magic: Earlier there was a false, useless shade; here there is real shade and real refreshment.
words.grammar: Two broken plurals joined by “and.”
words.why: The pair paints comfort through climate and water together.
words.note: Hell had smoke without shelter; paradise has shade with water.

words.root: Fruits, pleasant produce, delightful things enjoyed
words.magic: The plural suggests variety and abundance.
words.grammar: Broken plural in the accusative.
words.why: Fruit means ease, sweetness and ready enjoyment.
words.note: Not one fruit basket — a whole world of choice.

words.root: Easy to swallow, pleasant, wholesome, enjoyed without trouble
words.magic: Food is not just allowed — it is enjoyed without fear or regret.
words.grammar: Adverbial accusative expressing manner.
words.why: It adds comfort and inner ease, not only taste.
words.note: Food that goes down with zero worry and total peace.

words.root: √j-z-y — repaying, rewarding, giving back what is due
words.magic: The surah balances warning with reward.
words.grammar: Present verb, first person plural.
words.why: Jazāʾ is measured repayment, perfectly fitting the deed.
words.note: Every act comes back wearing its true shape.

words.root: √ḥ-s-n — beauty, goodness, excellence
words.meaning: those who do good beautifully and well
words.magic: Not just avoiding wrong, but actively doing good with excellence.
words.grammar: Active participle plural, Form IV sense from aḥsana.
words.why: Iḥsān means beautiful excellence, higher than bare minimum goodness.
words.note: A muḥsin is the person who does the right thing in the best way.

words.root: √r-k-ʿ — bending, bowing low in humility
words.meaning: Bow! — a command to submit in prayer
words.magic: One short command exposes the stubbornness of those who still refuse.
words.grammar: Imperative plural.
words.why: Rukūʿ is a visible act of surrender.
words.note: The back bends when the ego should bend.

words.root: √ḥ-d-th — speech, narration, something newly brought forth
words.magic: The surah ends with a devastating question — if not this Qur'an, then what message will they believe?
words.grammar: Singular noun in the genitive after “which.”
words.why: It closes on the plainest possible word for speech, leaving no escape.
words.note: If truth this clear is rejected, what talk could ever work?
